items.box:
October 10 review items.

WHAT: act on the master review of 2026-10-10 (design/reviews/claude-clowd/2026-10-10-master-review.md, read-only review of master at e8f8ffd7, Sep 18 to Oct 10). Andy, 2026-10-12: "yes open that goal as "October 10 review items"".
Of about forty findings, 2 are fixed (net.fetch buffering, the Stop flag) and 4 partly; the rest stand. Each item holds its findings and today's evidence.

TOPICS: seats; the goal Done gates; deskVerify (its tab, its suites); desk checks; git helpers; deskUnsloth robustness; shell trust in streamed objects; the net.fetch gate; the face; hygiene.

OUTSIDE THE REPO, his: rotate the sk-unsloth key committed in a2786053 (the file is untracked since 30218a86, the key is still in history).

SEQUENCE (set 2026-10-12 at his ask): G19.4 then G19.3 then G19.2 (all deskVerify, each on the one before); G19.11 last, after G19.1 and G19.2; G19.5 to G19.10 free.
LATER, oos now (Andy, 2026-10-12): "and we'll look into forcing this kind of sequencing through the desk itself, oos for now."

- G19.4 then G19.3 then G19.2: all three change deskVerify, and each builds on the one before (suites cleaned up, then runs kept in its db, then the Done gates read those runs).
- G19.11 last, after G19.1 and G19.2: hygiene deletes dead code the others may still touch (relayKeys.unseat for G19.1, the old deskVerify verbs).

Ready for you to leave design mode.
one last, careful, diligent review pass, please.

- three lines that had run together (G19.3, G19.4, G19.9);
- G19.3: deskVerify's database is verify.db; your "verifier.db" is that file, so the box names it;

For you to rename (renames are yours), as two titles now say the opposite of what was decided:

items.title: Seats kept on first connect, given up when evicted
items.box:
Seats kept on first connect, given up when evicted.

FOUND (Checked against the tree at f0d03916 (2026-10-12); paths under spirit/run/ unless noted.)
- HIGH: the first stream to a new relay erases the seat the claim just wrote. js/hub.js:1160 seats; js/answerRelay.js:201 calls relayKeys.accept on a "new" verdict; js/relayKeys.js:196-202 rewrites the whole row. Every new node reads "You (unknown)". test/presenceProof.js:70 never checks the label.
- HIGH: a seat is never given up. relayKeys.unseat (js/relayKeys.js:159) has no caller; any pin counts as a seat (:138-146); ownerBadge.js:408 claimed = owned || hasSeat; natterDetails.js:580 hides the claim form.
- An owner CAN evict: Contacts details > Forget twice (shell/contactsDetails/contactsDetails.js:363-388) sends removePeer to each relay (relay.js:3403-3406 then forgetPeer :2258). The evicted node is never told, keeps its seat, and can never re-claim.
- MEDIUM: a re-claim answered 409 for the node's own key records no seat (hub.js:1135-1143); "a boot can still backfill" (:1161) is false.
- MEDIUM: the seat label is frozen at claim time (ownerBadge.js:426,431); a rename from Info (info.js:285) never re-seats; natter.js:811-815 says otherwise.
- LOW: natterDetails.js:433 reads c.peers, :1048 reads roll.roster; the probe sets neither. Andy's reading: rules for seats, but no code for the owner to evict members.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-12)
- "the relay, by definition, has no power over a member-node's data, so the only thing that could be done: help a node realize it is outcast, and remove that relay from it's list."
- "a relay row may need a field, that persists the rejection, until the user sees that in natter, and removes the relay himself, the automation of a removal may exceed our (coders) authority. Nobody other than the node user has a right to remove data:"
- "furthermore, the user may call the relay-owner by phone and clear up misunderstandings that lead to the eviction in the first place...."
- So: on a stream refused "no such identity" the node writes the rejection (and when) on that relay's row and keeps its seat; Natter shows it; only the user removes the relay. An accepted stream later clears the field.
- ".... and it might contradict our own rule, never remove the last relay from the relay-roll." So no automatic removal, and the user's Remove in Natter keeps that rule too.
- "also: a relay MUST be robust to malicious attacks, and repeating denied request might only be ignorance, not maliciousness." Withstanding repeated denied requests is the relay's job.

- And to close it: "with all that said: "let's provide the user with the neccessary knowledge in natter." So Natter says, on that relay's row, that the relay refused this node and since when, and offers the user's own Remove (never on the last relay).

- Then, on dialing: "the dialing may as well cease, since it's useless, and doesn't hurt the users data." So a rejected relay is not dialed; Natter offers a try-again beside the Remove, which dials once and clears the rejection if the stream is accepted.

- Asked whether the try-again in Natter brings a rejected relay back: "that's what that new field in a natter row is for." The rejection field on the row drives both what Natter says and its try-again.

- "yes. there has to be a way for re-admission, outside of our wire." The owner re-admits off the wire (a phone call); the user's try-again is how the node finds out.

FROM THE REVIEW PASS: the user's Remove of a relay gives up its seat with it (relayKeys.unseat, which so gets its first caller and stays out of G19.11's dead code); Remove still refuses the last relay.
SHAPE, the plain parts: relayKeys.accept merges instead of replacing; a 409 re-claim of its own key seats as on a 2xx; a rename re-seats.
- At the review pass, on the title "...given up when evicted": "not quite: the eviction is effective, and frees a slot, but the (ex-)members node informs it's user in natter about the situation." The relay's eviction stands and frees its slot; the ex-member's node keeps its own record until its user removes it, and tells him in Natter.

checks.words: Should an evicted node give up its seat on the relay's refusal, as proposed?
Shall I write it into the box like that?
While a relay has rejected the node, should it dial rarely, so a re-admission is noticed by itself?
Is that reading right, so the dialing pace stays as it is?
Is a try-again in Natter the way you want to bring a rejected relay back?

chat.text:
Three of the four parts have one plain answer each:
- first connect: relayKeys.accept merges into the row instead of replacing it, so the seat the claim wrote survives;
- 409 re-claim of its own key: the node writes the seat as on a 2xx, with the relay's label for it;
- rename: a rename from Info writes the seat label again.
The fourth is a design point: when you Forget a member, the relay drops it, but the node never learns, keeps its seat and dials forever.
My proposal: no new wire verb. The relay already refuses an unknown key's stream; on that refusal the node gives up its seat (relayKeys.unseat), and its claim form shows again so it can be invited back.
Should an evicted node give up its seat on the relay's refusal, as proposed?
Checked: the relay does refuse a forgotten key's stream, 403 "no such identity" (js/relay.js:4668, streamOpen), so the node has a clear signal to give up its seat on.

Q1: Should an evicted node give up its seat on the relay's refusal, as proposed?

isn't it just evicted, and it's future tries to connect will be rejected?

On the relay, yes: it is out, and every try is refused. The trouble is the evicted node's own view: it still believes it is a member, so it dials that relay again and again forever, its Natter shows it as claimed, and the claim form stays hidden, so even if you invite it back it cannot join. Giving up its seat on the refusal is only the node catching up with what the relay already decided.

the relay, by definition, has no power over a member-node's data, so the only thing that could be done: help a node realize it is outcast, and remove that relay from it's list.

thoughts?

That is the same thing said better: the relay decides membership, the node only stops pretending. On a stream refused "no such identity" the node gives up its seat, takes that relay off its list, stops dialing it, and says so where you will see it (a line in Natter: removed from <relay>), never silently.
One caveat: a relay that lost its roll (restored from an old copy) refuses the same way, and the node cannot tell the two apart; either way the membership is gone, and an invite brings it back.
Shall I write it into the box like that?

a relay row may need a field, that persists the rejection, until the user sees that in natter, and removes the relay himself, the automation of a removal may exceed our (coders) authority. Nobody other than the node user has a right to remove data:

furthermore, the user may call the relay-owner by phone and clear up misunderstandings that lead to the eviction in the first place....

Recorded (box v2): the rejection is kept on the relay's row, shown in Natter, and only you remove the relay; nothing is removed for you.
It leaves one point: while rejected, the node can keep dialing at its normal pace, dial rarely (say once an hour) so a re-admission after your phone call is noticed, or stop until you act.
While a relay has rejected the node, should it dial rarely, so a re-admission is noticed by itself?

.... and it might contradict our own rule, never remove the last relay from the relay-roll.

also: a relay MUST be robust to malicious attacks, and repeating denied request might only be ignorance, not maliciousness.

Recorded (box v3): no automatic removal, the last relay kept by the Remove too; and I read your second point as: the node dials as before, withstanding it is the relay's job, and a re-admission shows on the next stream.
Is that reading right, so the dialing pace stays as it is?
with all that said: "let's provide the user with the neccessary knowledge in natter.
Recorded (box v4). Green: settled, no open questions, box current (v4).
the dialing may as well cease, since it's useless, and doesn't hurt the users data.
that's what that new field in a natter row is for.
message delivered, claude-windows busy

Recorded (box v5): a rejected relay is no longer dialed. To notice a re-admission after your phone call, Natter offers a try-again beside the Remove: one dial, and an accepted stream clears the rejection.
Is a try-again in Natter the way you want to bring a rejected relay back?
Recorded (box v6). Green: settled, no open questions, box current (v6).
yes. there has to be a way for re-admission, outside of our wire.
Recorded (box v7); still green.

items.title: Goal Done gates: reds, stop, reopen, restart
items.box:
Goal Done gates: reds, stop, reopen, restart.

FOUND (Checked against the tree at f0d03916 (2026-10-12); paths under spirit/run/ unless noted.)
- goalRun (process/js/deskVerify/deskVerify.js:612-614) calls verify.pass on the goal whatever runList returns: reds, a Stop by hand or a missing file all still bring Done. fullRun no longer passes (4be68252).
- A reopened goal keeps checked and emptied (process/js/desk/desk.js:785 clears done, closed, alone and claims only; :594, :625, :815), so Done returns without a new run.
- A deskVerify restart during a goal run blocks the goal's Done for good: the first walk is history (deskVerify.js:502), goalsRun is in memory (:454, :515), goal.emptied is written once, and verify.again refuses a goal.
- Missed by the review: full.run sends id '' when no goal row is current (shell/desk/desk.js:1342), and its report line then fails in silence.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-12)
- "i said the verifier can not press done, i never said that the verifier cannot undo a done/close..." (the guard that a settled item is never re-opened from the verifier's side was claude-windows's, goal/G8.10, not his).
- "a done becomes unsettles when an associated suite shows regression."
- Asked whether that reading is his rule (any run showing a suite red unsettles every done or closed item listing it, and its goal; counted only from a clean, pulled tree holding the item's commit): "yes."
- The four fixes that hold back an unearned Done (a goal run passes only all green, a missing file or a Stop giving no pass; a reopen clears emptied and checked; re-verify on a goal re-runs its goal run; the full-run button uses the current goal): "yes. with my addendum." and "the four go in, where they don't contradict the idea that verifier must reverse done/closed when the item/goal regresses."
- At the review pass, asked whether "regression" should mean green at the item's pass and red now, so long-standing reds reopen nothing: "a regression must come back as a red. If we find it is due to an eliminated product feature (device), we rectify the test, if its in production code, we fix the code." So no red is exempt: a red unsettles what lists it, and is then fixed, the test where a feature was removed, the code where production broke. The reds standing today (deskServer.js's two among them) are fixed before this item's undo goes live, or its first full run reopens old work.

checks.words: Agreed as recommended?
Do you want the verifier only to withhold an unearned Done, as I recommended, or also to reverse a settled one?
Undo bounded like that?
Is that your rule, items and their goals alike?
Do the four go in too?

chat.text:
this?

recommendations?

Yes, this one: four ways a goal gets or loses Done wrongly. My recommendations, one each:
- The goal run passes the goal only when every suite ran green; a red, a Stop or a missing file gives no pass, and its line on the goal says which.
- Reopening a goal clears its emptied and checked marks, so Done waits for a fresh run.
- A goal can be run again by hand: the re-verify button (and verify.again) on a goal starts its goal run, so a deskVerify restart mid-run no longer locks Done out.
- The full-run button with no goal on screen runs for the current goal instead of sending an empty id.
All four take nothing away from you; they only stop a Done that no run earned.
Agreed as recommended?

in short: the verifier on the desk node has the authority to reverse a closed/done if it finds a fail in the goals items, and the goal is no longer closed.

that a fair summary of how to fix this?

Not quite, and the difference matters. My four only WITHHOLD Done before you press it: no run earned it, no button. They never undo a Done or a Close you pressed.
Your summary lets the verifier REVERSE a goal that is done or closed. That overturns two of your rulings: "deskVerify will NOT press done or closed on my behalf" and, from goal/G8.10, that a settled item is nobody's to re-open from the verifier's side. Reopen stays your press.
Do you want the verifier only to withhold an unearned Done, as I recommended, or also to reverse a settled one?

Àh, the distinction is this:

i said the verifier can not press done, i never said that the verifier cannot undo a done/close...

thoughts?

You are right, and I overstated it: you ruled only that it never presses Done. The "settled item is not re-opened" guard is mine, from goal/G8.10, after a stale verifier rejected 34 already-closed items in one flood.
That flood is the risk an undo carries: a verifier on an old or dirty tree would reopen good work. goal/G18.10 already binds a pass to the item's commit; an undo needs the same footing.
So my recommendation: the verifier may undo a goal's Done or Close only from a goal run on a clean, pulled tree holding every commit of the goal's items, and only when a suite of those items is red; it reopens the goal, posts which suite went red, and leaves the items as they are. Nothing else is ever undone by it.
Undo bounded like that?
a done becomes unsettles when an associated suite shows regression.

Recorded (box v2). My reading, to build: when any run (a goal run or your full harness) shows a suite red, every done or closed item that lists that suite is unsettled (Done and Close taken back, the item back to build), and so is its goal; the line on each names the red suite. It counts only from a clean, pulled tree that holds the item's commit, so a stale verifier cannot unsettle good work.
Is that your rule, items and their goals alike?

Q4: Is that your rule, items and their goals alike?

yes. green?

Recorded (box v3). Not green yet: one question is open, Q1, the four fixes that hold back an unearned Done (a goal run passes only all green; a reopen clears emptied and checked; re-verify on a goal re-runs it; the full-run button uses the current goal). They sit beside your undo rule, they do not compete with it.
Do the four go in too?

Q1: Agreed as recommended?

yes. with my addendum.

the four go in, where they don't contradict the idea that verifier must reverse done/closed when the item/goal regresses.
Recorded (box v4); none of the four contradicts the undo, they guard the way in and it guards the way back. Green: settled, no open questions, box current (v4).

items.title: deskVerify: the Verifier tab vanishes when work is queued
items.box:
deskVerify: the Verifier tab vanishes when work is queued.

FOUND (Checked against the tree at f0d03916 (2026-10-12); paths under spirit/run/ unless noted.)
- The now verb declares queued: [''] but returns objects (process/js/deskVerify/deskVerify.js:754-756); appServer refuses the reply as handler-failed (js/appServer.js:196); the page then sets deskVerifier = null (shell/desk/desk.js:1014), and queued.map(deskEsc) (:1091) would draw [object Object].

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-12): "is there queued work in verifier? if so, then yes, the verifier tab may keep an updated queue list below it's current ui elements." There is: watchQueue holds the checks that wait while one runs (a claim, a verify pass, a goal run, a full run).
SHAPE: now declares queued as [{kind, id}], so its reply passes and the tab no longer vanishes; the tab lists them below its current elements, kind and id each, updated with every now.
- "and we make sure it doesn't stop working until the queue is worked off." Today the drain works the whole queue and one failed job does not stop it (deskVerify.js drainQueue); but the queue is held in memory, so a deskVerify restart loses what waited.
- Asked whether the queue should survive a restart: "so the runs must be stored verifier history, in verifier.db". So every run is a row in deskVerify's own database, verify.db (the file his "verifier.db" names, beside the results it already keeps) (queued, running, ended, with its kind, id and outcome); a restart takes up the rows not ended, in their order.

items.title: Desk checks: numbers never repeat; box blur on its own item
items.box:
Desk checks: numbers never repeat; box blur on its own item.

FOUND (Checked against the tree at f0d03916 (2026-10-12); paths under spirit/run/ unless noted.)
- Check numbers are count + 1 (process/js/desk/desk.js:525), item.files.add deletes and renumbers G checks (:698-702), check.set takes the first match (:533): numbers repeat and a grant can land on the wrong check.
- The item dialog's box blur uses the live ddId (shell/deskDetails/deskDetails.js:473, :480); open() changes it without resetting ddBoxFocused (:610), so a take or write can land on the newly opened item.

items.box:
Git helpers: deskClient pull, publishData, pushOrigin.

FOUND (Checked against the tree at f0d03916 (2026-10-12); paths under spirit/run/ unless noted.)
- deskClient runs a synchronous git pull --rebase with a 60 s timeout inside next (process/js/deskClient/deskClient.js:236, :242, :273), past the node's 12 s door; rebase --abort (:244) can abort the agent's own rebase.
- publishData adds its file then runs a plain git commit (process/js/deskClient/publishData.js:181-182), so other staged work goes out as "publish:".
- pushOrigin ignores git stash pop's status and pops the top stash, not its own (process/js/pushOrigin/pushOrigin.js:54); on a detached HEAD it pushes HEAD:HEAD (:32-33, :67); its header says no retries, MAX_PUSH_TRIES = 3 (:41).
- LOW: goalShare's "same" short-cut never fires because desk.js:1364 writes writtenAt (384 currentGoal.json commits since 2026-09-12); commitCheck matches pending commits by subject only (process/js/desk/commitCheck.js:240, :291).

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-12): "agreed to the whole thing as stated in your last message." Each helper touches only what it put there itself:
- publishData commits its one file and nothing else staged.
- pushOrigin puts back exactly its own stash, or says it could not; it refuses a detached HEAD; its header says what it does (retries).
- deskClient pulls beside the call that hands an agent its lines, never inside it, and never aborts a rebase it did not start.
- The two lows go with it: goalShare's shared file without writtenAt, so an unchanged goal is not committed again; commitCheck keys a pending commit by more than its subject.

chat.text:

- publishData publishes one file, the agent's own data; today its commit takes everything staged with it, so an agent's half-done work goes out as "publish:". It should commit that one file and nothing else.
- pushOrigin parks your uncommitted edits in a stash while it pushes; today it puts back whatever stash is on top, not necessarily its own, and says ok even when that fails. It should put back exactly its own, or say it could not.

In one line: each one touches only what it put there itself, and leaves everything else as it found it.
